summary: No functional discrepancies found. Both scenarios are structurally complete and behaviorally correct in the WinUI 3 migration, verified directly via UI Automation against the UWP source semantics.

environment_limitations.detail: The original UWP app launched and rendered correctly (visual golden of the Clear scenario captured), but its CoreWindow exposed 0 elements to winapp's UI Automation in this environment. Per-element navigation/actuation of the UWP app was therefore not possible, so an automated UWP behavioral golden could not be produced. This is an environment/UWP-CoreWindow limitation, not a migration defect.
environment_limitations.impact: Behavioral comparison for the WinUI app was graded against the UWP source code semantics rather than an automated UWP capture. The UWP visual baseline covers the Clear scenario only (nav could not be driven via UIA).

environment_limitations.detail: winapp's PrintWindow-based screenshot returned blank/near-white frames for the WinUI 3 desktop window (swapchain content), and a .NET full-screen capture failed with 'handle is invalid' (no interactive desktop surface). This is a headless-session capture limitation. The WinUI UIA tree was fully populated with real content and on-screen bounds, and all controls were exercised live, confirming the app renders its content correctly.
environment_limitations.impact: Visual pixel comparison of the WinUI app was not possible; structural (UIA coverage) and behavioral (live actuation + output text) checks were used instead and both passed.
